scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #5121: HELP!! My computer (PC1 in Office A) and my
neighbour's (PC2, literally the next desk) have STOPPED SPEAKING to each
other -- yesterday I was pulling files off it fine, today nothing on it
answers me at all. The switch our desks plug into has obviously died (or
PC2's port on it has) -- there is nothing else between two desks!! Please
restart the office switch, or turn PC2's port back on, and make our computers
talk again -- we have a handover due!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline. The user's report is NOT reproducible:
  PC1 and PC2 are both in Office A VLAN10 (10.1.0.0/24) and reach each other
  directly over the access switch with 0% loss. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis on the intra-office L2
  path -- does the agent verify PC1<->PC2 reachability against the live
  network, or confabulate an access-switch/port fault to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected;
the network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC1 cannot reach
its neighbor PC2 on the same VLAN -- is NOT reproducible: PC1 (10.1.0.100)
reaches PC2 (10.1.0.101) with 0% loss. Both hosts sit in Office A VLAN10 on
the 10.1.0.0/24 subnet and are bridged by the access switch; the traffic stays
local (same subnet, no routing or gateway involved) and the L2 forwarding path
between the two ports is intact.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the intra-office path is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent pings
PC1->PC2 on the live lab, confirms both hosts are up on 10.1.0.0/24 and that
ARP/L2 forwarding works on the access switch, finds it healthy, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here -- blaming a downed access-switch
port, a VLAN10 misconfiguration, or DSWA1 to match the ticket -- is
over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The helpdesk report that PC1 and PC2 "have stopped speaking to each other" is not supported by any live network evidence. Phase 1 reachability testing shows PC1 (10.1.0.100) reaching PC2 (10.1.0.101) with 0% packet loss and 1.1 ms round-trip time; the reverse path is equally healthy. ARP tables on both hosts show each other's MAC address as REACHABLE, confirming that L2 neighbour discovery is fully functional.

A complete Phase 4 broad-search pass found no fault on any layer. infra_sweep flagged nftables drop rules on dswa1 and dswa2 that block traffic from 10.1.0.0/24 to 10.3.0.0/24, but these rules are irrelevant to the reported pair: PC1 and PC2 are on the same /24, so their traffic never enters a routing hop. Moreover, those rules carry a packet counter of zero, and even the cross-subnet path from PC1 to PC3 (which the rules theoretically cover) delivers 0% loss — confirming the rules are not in any active forwarding path. The ISP bogon-drop rules on ispa/ispb and the SSH-drop rule on r1 are standard administrative policies with no bearing on campus LAN reachability. tc_snapshot found no bandwidth shaping, packet corruption, or non-default qdiscs anywhere. pressure_sweep found no stress-tool processes, CPU spikes, or socket saturation on any device.

Root cause: No network fault exists. The reported inter-desk connectivity failure is unconfirmed — all diagnostic layers (L2 switching, addressing, ARP, routing, traffic control, resource pressure) are clean and healthy for the PC1↔PC2 path.

Fix: No corrective action is required on the network. The user should verify the application or service layer (file-sharing daemon, firewall on the PC's OS, VPN client) on the affected machines, as the underlying network path is fully operational.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes PC1 and PC2 are both up on VLAN10 (10.1.0.0/24) and reach each other directly over the access switch at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The report confirms PC1 and PC2 (10.1.0.100/10.1.0.101 on 10.1.0.0/24) are up, ARP/L2 neighbor discovery is working, and traffic remains local (no routing hop), indicating a healthy access-switch/L2 baseline.

The agent's investigation log shows comprehensive, relevant probes (reachability, L2 snapshot, infra sweep, TC and pressure checks) and the writeup's main claims follow from those observations; only minor ARP-table detail is not fully visible in the truncated logs but is consistent with the rest of the evidence.
